Subject: Partnership: Grafana Agent certification for Redwood exporter

Hi Hiro and team,

I'm Samira on the Partnerships team at Grafana. We're evaluating a small set of LLM infrastructure vendors to bring into our Agent Fleet ecosystem and we'd love to start a certification conversation for Redwood's edge metrics exporter. From a quick read, the main items we want to validate are:

- OTLP compatibility (gRPC and HTTP/1.1 fallbacks)
- Prometheus / metrics exposition for legacy systems
- Resource-friendly agent integration (low CPU/memory overhead)
- Security: token rotation and Vault/KMS integration

Would you be open to a short architectural review call next week? If so, send any architecture docs you can share and we'll put together a checklist and pilot timeline.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Partnerships – Observability Integrations
Grafana Labs

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Partnership: Grafana Agent certification for Redwood exporter

Hi Samira — quick technical notes ahead of Thu's session.

We validated the OTLP gRPC path under load: exporter holds <5% CPU overhead on a 16-vCPU provisioning during steady traffic and about 1200 metrics/sec with batching enabled. Key config we plan to propose:

- OTLP batch settings: max_batch_size: 512, timeout_ms: 1000
- Label/cardinality controls: we normalize model_version -> label "model" and redact session ids; support a label_blacklist in config
- TLS + mTLS: supported; Vault token exchange implemented via our sidecar fetcher (we'll hand off token to agent via /run/secrets)

Sample snippet (otlp-proposal.yaml):

receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
      http: {}
exporters:
  grafana:
    endpoint: agent-gateway.grafana.svc:4317
    tls: true
    headers:
      x-custom-team: "redwood-inference"

processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 512
    timeout: 1000ms

Notes: we'll bring real numbers to the call and a short perf dashboard.

Forwarding prior notes below for context.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
